title: Constructions and Tilings: Polygon Angles and Tessellations

standard_text: Constructing regular polygons, the angle sum of polygons, interior and exterior angles of regular polygons, and tilings (tessellations) of the plane (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 Constructions and Tilings worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 6): angle sum of polygons, regular polygon angles, which shapes tile and angles at a point. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Angles meeting at a point in a tiling add up to 360°
key_sub: Angle sum of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°.
body_html:
How it works

A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles, so its angles add up to (n − 2) × 180°. In a regular polygon each interior angle is this ÷ n, and each exterior angle is 360° ÷ n.

In a tiling, the angles that meet at a point add up to 360°. Only equilateral triangles (60°), squares (90°) and regular hexagons (120°) tile on their own.

Example

Find each interior angle of a regular octagon.

(8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°

1,080° ÷ 8

Answer: 135°

Example

Two regular octagons meet at a point. What else fits?

360° − 270° = 90°

Answer: A square

Common mistakes

  • Using n × 180° for the angle sum.
  • Mixing up interior and exterior angles.
  • Thinking regular pentagons can tile a floor.

faq.q: What is the angle sum of a polygon?
Which regular polygons tile the plane?
faq.a: Only equilateral triangles, squares and regular hexagons, because 60°, 90° and 120° divide 360° exactly.
